Welcome
We are a small village school in the beautiful village of Redmarley, where the pupils are at the centre of everything we do.
We are a Church of England school and so have a strong relationship with our local church. We have regular church services that our parents and families attend and our lovely vicar visits us regularly to support our RE curriculum and lead Collective Worship.
Our Vision is 'Shine as a Light in the World' and our curriculum provides our children with a wealth of opportunities to do this. We have weekly visits from a music specialist, sports coach and gymnastic teacher, which provides an extra enrichment to our curriculum in addition to the quality daily teaching experience they receive. It is our aim to enable our children to 'shine' in learning, developing their talents and achievements as they grow throughout their time with us. We want children to be happy and thriving, so that when they leave us they are ready for the next stage of their education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Values | Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Our Values
As a Church of England school, we keep Christian values at the heart of what we do.
Every half term, we learn about a different Christian value. We use Roots and Fruits as a Christian Collective Worship resource over a two year period. Rooted in Bible teaching there are 12 Christian Values which we focus on one per half term. The values link with the season of the Church year.
We think about these values as part of our daily worship, where we reflect upon the teachings of Jesus. We also try hard to achieve these values both at home and in school.
Our Worship Board
We have a working wall in our school hall where we record any ideas or thinking from our worship. This provides opportunities for reflection throughout the school day as we can all refer to it.
We have a Worship Book where we record adult and child responses. This helps us to evaluate the impact of worship.
Reflection areas
Every class in school has their own reflection area. We can come here to think about our value and write or draw our ideas, to look at a Bible, or to have some quiet reflection.
Stars of the Week
Each week, teachers nominate one child from their class who has lived out our Christian Vision and values. The children’s pictures are then displayed in the hall, and certificates are sent home.
At the end of each term a child is nominated from each class who has consistently shown our Christian vision and values. They are awarded a 'golden star pin' to symbolise that they are 'Shining as a Light in the World'.
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School

pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Our latest SIAMS report
Our latest SIAMS inspection was in February 2026. The inspector highlighted the following notable strengths:
The vision inspires ambition and fosters a strong sense of belonging across Redmarley Church of England Primary School. Leaders live out the vision with pride, empowering pupils to share their gifts.
Pupils considered to be vulnerable receive personalised support that enables them to thrive academically, socially, emotionally and personally. This inclusive offer reflects the school’s commitment to dignity and equity.
An inclusive approach nurtures a culture of care, collaboration and shared purpose among pupils, staff and families. This collective commitment strengthens community relationships and promotes holistic flourishing shaped by the school’s Christian foundation.
The trust’s vision effectively grows capacity through shared responsibility. Consideration of wellbeing and pupil needs ensures sustainable improvement, enhancing the school’s overall effectiveness.
Develop opportunities for pupils and adults to grow spiritually throughout the curriculum. This is to ensure spiritual development is intentional and consistent, building on existing strengths.
Deepen pupils’ understanding of justice and responsibility and expand opportunities to actively live out these values. This is to maximise their ability to make ethical choices and take meaningful action.
Please click below to see our report in full
Redmarley C of E Primary School Academy SIAMS report February 2026.
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School

pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development
At Redmarley Church of England Academy, Christian values are firmly embedded in the daily life of our school. As a Church school, we approach Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development (SMSCD) from a Christian perspective, offering a holistic approach to education.
The Church school offers a spiritual and moral basis for the development of human wholeness and a sure foundation for personal and social values based on the person and ministry of Christ. A distinctive language is provided for the understanding of life and interpreting human experience. As a community of faith, the Church School should, in its best expression, reflect the nature of the Trinity, a life shared and defined by reference to others. Here we can begin to discover who we are, why we are, and perhaps most importantly what we might be.
The Way Ahead, Chapter 3 para 3.26
SMSCD is about developing the whole child through:
in an environment which enables all pupils to grow and flourish, become confident individuals and appreciate their own worth and that of others.
Our school promotes Christian fellowship and a caring and compassionate community, where pupils are able to reflect upon a world filled with awe and wonder.
Spiritual Development - 'This language of spirituality begins from the Christian understanding that everyone is a valued creation, individually and uniquely made by God, like pots made by a potter (Isaiah 64:8). Yet in life things happen that impact on the physical ‘pot’ of life and create cracks that provide a glimpse of ‘something’ beyond the tangible.' - Diocese of Gloucester.
Spirituality Statement
'We take joy in the wows, we work through our ows and make time for the nows.'.
Social Development -
Cultural Development -
See our SMSCD policy for further information (below)
British Values Statement
At Redmarley Primary Academy we value and respect different cultures, religions and beliefs. We celebrate and share diversity as a school, and our school curriculum provides a wealth of opportunity to explore this further in different contexts. Here is a sample of what we teach in relation to promoting British Values:
The 5 Fundamental British Values
The ability to understand and communicate are the most important areas of learning. We ensure that pupils are given a ‘voice’ to communicate. This ‘voice’ could be using words, objects, photographs, pictures, symbols or other means. We empower our pupils by giving them opportunities to make choices about things which are important to them. Pupil Voice is heard through Collective Worship group, School Council and individual class groups. Pupil voice also feeds into our School Development Plan.
Pupils are helped to learn to manage their behaviour and take responsibility for their actions. We involve pupils in setting rules of behaviour e.g. behaviour in their classroom and Worship; helping pupils to make decisions and choices that are acceptable to the school community and society at large. We support pupils in understanding that everyone has a responsibility and that there are consequences when rules are broken. They recognise that whilst we have rules at school, other rules and laws exist in the country for the same reasons. Staff are committed to providing a consistent and safe environment within the setting. Visits from authorities such as the Local Authority Services, Police and Fire Service are encouraged.
Pupils are encouraged to become good and valued citizens. We do this by supporting each pupil to become as independent as possible and encourage them to help and support each other. We endeavour to demonstrate that everyone has rights; this includes the right to say 'Yes' or 'No' to ideas or activities.
Part of our motto is 'respect' and this also forms part of our behaviour approach. This was chosen by all stakeholders as an essential value for 'getting on' in the world. Respect is unpicked and explored in Collective Worship and class; the pupils are shown examples of this and are encouraged to be reflective and responsive to this in practice.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs:
We are a Christian school, who as part of our ethos are tolerant and respectful of different faiths and beliefs. Within our RE syllabus and throughout our curriculum the pupils are provided with learning opportunities around others.

pageCache.pageTitle: Worship | Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Worship
Worship at Redmarley C. of E. Primary Academy aims to reflect the essential features within the rich traditions of Anglican prayer and Worship, whilst developing the individual, in accordance with the school’s aims and values.
Pupils are given the opportunity to consider the Bible as a source of inspiration and learning. They are encouraged to reflect upon Christian Symbols and their use in worship; to observe the cycle of the Anglican year, to participate in the regularity and set order of Anglican Worship, to learn traditional responses and prayers, and to discover the value of silence and reflection within the context of Christian Worship.
Organisation
To provide pupils with variety in their experience of worship, acts of worship may take the form of a whole school act of worship for all pupils or separate acts of worship for pupils in different age groups, classes or school groups.
We hold Collective Worship everyday from 9.00am - 9.20am. Each day it is led by a different member of staff or our Class 4 Worship Leaders.
At special times of the year, e.g. Easter, Christmas, Harvest Festival, or leaving day for Year 6, we invite parents and friends to join us in worship as this promotes the community spirit of the school and is a practical demonstration of the way that home and school work together to support the achievements of our children and uphold the schools values.
Children also attend Church services at other times under parental supervision – Meeting Point services, Mothering Sunday, Christingle, Christmas Celebrations and Carol Services.
Please see our Collective Worship Policy for more information.
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values | Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
British Values
Teaching and Promoting British Values
The DfE have recently reinforced the need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
At Redmarley these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Democracy
Each year the children decide upon their class rules. All the children contribute to the drawing up of the rules. We have a school council which meets regularly with the Headteacher or Senior Teacher to discuss issues raised in class council meetings. The council has its own budget and is genuinely able to effect change within the school. Every child on the student council is voted in by their class.
Children have an annual questionnaire where they are able to put forward their views about the school.
The Rule of Law
The importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced at Redmarley. Pupils are taught from an early age the rules of the school.
Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind rules and laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service help reinforce this message.
Individual Liberty
At Redmarley, pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make informed choices, through a safe environment and an empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our e-Safety and PSHE lessons. They also understand that with rights come responsibilities.
Mutual Respect
Mutual respect is at the heart of our values. Children learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
At Redmarley we actively promote diversity through our celebrations of different faiths and cultures. Religious Education lessons and PSHE lessons reinforce messages of tolerance and respect for others. The children visit places of worship that are important to different faiths. As a school we work closely with families from different faiths in order to ensure that all children are included
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision and Aims | Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Our Vision and Aims
“You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden. 15 Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house. 16 In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.
The bible tells us to let our light shine among people (Matthew 5). At Redmarley Primary Academy we learn how to shine our light in the world through respect, perseverance and recognition of our achievements: sharing our talents with others.
Our motto has been chosen to support and enable our pupils to 'Shine as a Light in the World'. We take inspiration for our motto from the bible and teachings of Jesus Christ:
Respect: Pupils need to respect (God, family, themselves, friends, school, church, village, national and global community). The bible teaches us that it is important to respect and love others (regardless of station) through Jesus washing his Disciples feet.
Persevere: Pupils need to learn how important it is to 'keep going' and have faith that this enable them to succeed (even when failure occurs). Noah's challenge to build an ark exemplifies the importance of faith, commitment and perseverance.
Achieve: Pupils need to find success (academically, personally, socially and spiritually) and this gives a strong sense of achievement. Through trusting in God, Christians find the strength to achieve: I can do all things through him who strengthens me. Philippians 4:13.
At Redmarley C of E Primary Academy the staff and local advisors provide our pupils with the best education that we can; one that excites, engages and motivates them to become independent, lifelong learners. Within our Christian setting we aim to provide a secure, caring and happy environment where our pupils will feel confident to achieve their full potential.
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Pre-School | Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Welcome to RPA Pre-School
Our school is proud to offer a Pre-school facility for children starting from the age of 3, subject to availability. Please note that children MUST be in their "Pre-School ' year.
Our Pre-school is integrated into Class 1 along with our Reception children. The classroom is designed with dedicated zones that provide an engaging and fun learning environment, allowing children to explore and understand the world around them.
We have a garden area equipped with a mud kitchen, loose parts, digging areas, water play, and opportunities to develop gross motor skills. These spaces are designed to ensure children can run, play, and explore safely and joyfully.
Attending our Pre-school will give your child a seamless entry into reception, as they will already be familiar with the routines and systems.
Play is central to our curriculum, complemented by small group work that lays a solid foundation for their future education. Children build strong relationships with our staff, boosting their confidence and independence as they prepare for reception.
We emphasise the three prime areas of development: personal, social and emotional, physical, and creative. These areas are crucial for early learning and are supported through activities that enhance communication, language, and literacy skills. Our resources are designed to be accessible and adaptable to support each child's progression.
Our Safeguardign Lead for the setting is Mrs Laura Hankins (Headteacher) and Miss Charlotte Rimmer (Assistant Headteacher). Please visit the school Safeguarding page for more information.
Children do not need to be fully toilet trained, though we recommend avoiding nappies due to limited changing facilities. Pull-ups are a better option if needed.
We accept Early Years funding of both 15 & 30 hours, subject to entitlement through HMRC.
Additional hours are available at £7.50 per hour, invoiced at the end of the month.
For lunch, children can bring a packed lunch from home or opt for hot school dinners.
Snacks, including fruit, milk, and toast/crackers, are provided.
For more details or to discuss any additional needs your child may have, please contact Mrs Julie Watkins at admin@redmarley.gloucs.sch.uk to arrange a meeting with our Class 1 teacher (Miss Emily Davies) or Headteacher (Mrs Laura Hankins) and Preschool Lead (Miss Alana Salter)
You can find further information in our Pre-school handbook below and on our Class 1 page. We are proud to offer a fantastic start to your child's school journey at Redmarley.
We look forward to welcoming your child to our vibrant and nurturing Pre-school setting.
Emily Davies Alana Salter
Head Teacher (Early Year's Lead)

Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Music
Intent
At Redmarley Academy, we believe that every child is musical and should have the opportunity to develop a lifelong love and appreciation of music. Through our music curriculum, we aim to inspire pupils to become confident performers, composers and listeners, whilst developing creativity, self-expression and a sense of achievement.
We use the Kapow Primary Music Scheme to deliver the National Curriculum for Music. The curriculum provides a progressive, knowledge-rich approach that enables children to develop musical understanding through singing, listening, performing, improvising and composing. Pupils encounter a wide range of musical styles, genres, traditions and cultures, helping them develop respect and appreciation for music from around the world.
Music at Redmarley Academy goes beyond the National Curriculum. We enhance our provision through our partnership with Make Music Gloucestershire, providing pupils with opportunities to learn and perform on tuned instruments as part of whole-class instrumental teaching. We further enrich musical experiences through:
We want our pupils to leave Redmarley Academy with:
Rocksteady music sessions
School choir
Piano tuition
Singing assemblies
Performance opportunities throughout the year
School, community and celebratory events
A love and appreciation of music.
Implementation
Music is taught through the Kapow Primary Music Scheme, which provides full coverage of the National Curriculum and follows a carefully sequenced progression model.
The curriculum is designed as a spiral curriculum, where pupils revisit key concepts and skills throughout their primary education.
This approach ensures:
The curriculum develops the following strands throughout all year groups:
Children build their musical knowledge and skills through:
Performing
Listening
Composing
The history of music
The inter-related dimensions of music
Playing tuned and untuned instruments
Improvisation
Composition
Listening and appraising
Performance opportunities
Lesson structure
Each lesson follows a clear sequence to support effective learning and retention:
Retrieval and Recall
Lessons begin by revisiting prior learning through short retrieval activities. These activities strengthen long-term memory, reinforce key concepts and help pupils make meaningful connections between previous and new learning.
Attention Grabber
An engaging activity introduces the lesson and generates curiosity. This may take the form of a discussion, musical stimulus, question or investigation.
Main Learning
Children participate in a variety of musical activities through:
Teacher modelling
Guided practice
Independent application
Collaborative learning
Practical musical experiences
Reflection and Review
Lessons conclude with opportunities for children to reflect on their learning, discuss key concepts and evaluate their own progress.
Adaptive Teaching and SEND
At Redmarley Academy, we are committed to ensuring that all pupils can access and succeed in music.
Kapow's adaptive teaching guidance is embedded throughout planning, ensuring lessons are accessible for all learners through:
The carefully sequenced curriculum avoids large jumps in complexity and enables all pupils, including those with SEND, to build confidence and make strong progress from their starting points.
Scaffolding and graduated support
Multi-sensory approaches
Clear instructions and structured tasks
Collaborative and independent learning opportunities
Enrichment
We believe musical experiences should extend beyond classroom lessons. In addition to curriculum music, pupils benefit from:
These experiences help children develop confidence, resilience and a sense of pride in their musical achievements.
The impact of our music curriculum is seen through confident, enthusiastic and engaged pupils who develop both musical skills and an appreciation of music in all its forms.
By the time children leave Redmarley Academy, they will have:
We evaluate the impact of our curriculum through:
Successful outcomes are evident when pupils can talk confidently about their learning, perform with increasing musicality, demonstrate secure musical knowledge and show enthusiasm for participating in musical activities.
Ultimately, we aim for pupils to leave Redmarley Academy as confident young musicians who recognise the value of music in their lives, appreciate the rich diversity of musical traditions and possess the skills and confidence to continue their musical journey in the future.

Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Art and Design
Intent
At Redmarley Primary Academy, we place great importance on Art and Design as a means of developing creativity, self-expression and cultural understanding. We aim to engage, inspire and challenge pupils through a curriculum that develops artistic skills, knowledge and vocabulary while fostering imagination, curiosity and individuality.
We use the Kapow Art and Design scheme as the foundation of our curriculum. Kapow's carefully sequenced curriculum provides clear progression in knowledge, skills and vocabulary through a spiral curriculum model. This ensures that pupils revisit key concepts and artistic techniques throughout their primary education, building on prior learning and developing increasing depth, confidence and sophistication over time.
Our curriculum focuses on 5 strands:
There are then four key discipline areas :
It is through these disciplines that pupils develop their ability to generate ideas, use sketchbooks effectively, apply and refine practical skills, understand the work of artists and designers, and evaluate and analyse artistic work.
Whilst Kapow provides the progression framework, teachers use their professional judgement to adapt learning contexts and outcomes to reflect pupils' interests, local experiences and wider curriculum themes. This ensures learning remains meaningful and engaging whilst maintaining the ambitious progression of knowledge, skills and vocabulary expected for each year group.
For example, when pupils study the Romans in History, they may explore Roman mosaics through an art project. Whilst creating mosaic designs, pupils develop the artistic skills, techniques and vocabulary identified within the Kapow progression, such as pattern, tessellation, composition, colour and shape. In this way, pupils deepen both their historical understanding and artistic development through purposeful cross-curricular learning.
Through studying a diverse range of artists, craftspeople and designers from different cultures, historical periods and artistic traditions, pupils develop an appreciation of how Art and Design reflects, shapes and enriches society.
Our Art and Design curriculum is underpinned by Kapow's progressive and carefully structured scheme of work. The spiral curriculum design ensures that:
Teachers use Kapow's progression maps to ensure consistent coverage of the key artistic disciplines alongside the progressive development of:
Lessons are practical, exploratory and skills-focused. Pupils are encouraged to experiment with a wide range of materials and techniques, take creative risks, reflect upon their work and refine their ideas over time. Sketchbooks are used as working documents where pupils can explore techniques, record observations, develop ideas and demonstrate progression.
At Redmarley, we recognise that no two cohorts are the same. Teachers therefore adapt projects, themes and artistic outcomes to suit the interests, experiences and needs of their pupils. This adaptation does not dilute the curriculum; rather, it enhances engagement and provides meaningful contexts through which pupils can apply the carefully sequenced knowledge and skills within the Kapow framework.
The Kapow scheme is fully adaptable for pupils with SEND and supports our commitment to inclusive practice. Every lesson includes adaptive teaching strategies, enabling all pupils to access and succeed within the curriculum. These include:
The step-by-step progression within the curriculum helps avoid unnecessary jumps in complexity and supports pupils, particularly those with SEND, to develop confidence and independence as artists.
Teachers explicitly model artistic techniques, teach subject-specific vocabulary and use high-quality Kapow resources, including specialist videos and professional guidance, to ensure teaching is accurate, engaging and ambitious.
The impact of our Art and Design curriculum is evident in the enthusiasm, creativity and confidence demonstrated by our pupils. Children are highly engaged because artistic learning is connected to topics, experiences and interests that are relevant and meaningful to them, whilst remaining firmly rooted in the progression of knowledge, skills and vocabulary outlined within the Kapow curriculum.
Pupils demonstrate clear progression in their artistic abilities as they move through the school. They can confidently discuss artistic techniques, processes and artists using appropriate subject-specific vocabulary and are increasingly able to evaluate, refine and improve their own work.
Through the spiral curriculum, pupils retain and build upon previously taught knowledge and skills, leading to increasingly sophisticated artistic outcomes. Sketchbooks and finished pieces provide evidence of progression in creativity, technical skill and artistic understanding over time.
By linking art to wider curriculum themes, local opportunities and enrichment experiences, pupils understand that Art and Design is relevant beyond the classroom. Through workshops, visiting artists, educational visits and creative projects, children gain an appreciation of the role that art plays in shaping cultures, communities and the wider world.
At Redmarley, Kapow provides the progression and structure, whilst teachers provide the context. This ensures our curriculum remains ambitious, inclusive and engaging, enabling every child to develop as a creative, knowledgeable and confident artist.

Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
English - Reading at RPA
Unlocking the joys of reading opens the world to children. It provides a mirror, allowing children to better understand themselves and all that they do; it also provides a window, where children can learn about the world through experiences they may not encounter. It is our intent at Redmarley Primary Academy that children are strong, joyful readers, who are able to learn through reading.
Reading is a complex, problem solving exercise is does not come instinctively but needs to be carefully taught, applied and nurtured. The Reading House Model (EEF), effectively captures this:
Early Reading and Phonics
Early reading is children's first foray into books. This happens from birth, where parents begin to share stories as their child grows (from simple visuals to increasingly sophisticated stories as a child's understanding and comprehension develops). School then continues this journey. This involves teaching children to decode the alphabetic and phonetic code to be able to put sounds to letters, as well as continuing to build children's reading understanding and comprehension (through sharing and talking about stories, rhymes and songs).
Use one systematic synthetic phonics programme (SSP) in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2
At Redmarley, we teach phonics using the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revisited Programme. We believe that for all our children to become fluent readers and writers, phonics must be taught through a systematic and structured phonics programme. In phonics lessons, we teach children that the letters of the alphabet represent a different sound, that these can be used in a variety of combinations and are put together to make words. The children learn to recognise all of the different sounds and combinations that they might see when they are reading or writing.
We introduce children to the phonics programme in Nursery and the programme finishes by the Spring term of Year 2 or when an assessment has shown that children have a secure understanding of Phase 5 phonics.
Foundations for Phonics in Nursery

If you are a parent and would like more information about how to support your child with phonics at home, please follow this link to find the Reception and Year 1 overview as well as videos of the sound pronunciations, letter formation sheets and other helpful resources. https://www.littlewandlelettersandsounds.org.uk/resources/for-parents/
Once basic phonics and decoding is 'mastered', we support children to continue to develop as readers, so that they become increasingly fluent and prosodic as word readers and develop good comprehension alongside this. Phonics never 'goes away' and continues to be hugely relevant and an important strategy children and adults use to decode unfamiliar words they encounter,
Children have regular opportunities to practise their reading in class, whether this is aloud, part of guided reading or reading quietly to themselves or an adult. Children's reading books are matched to their ability through the Accelerated Reader scheme. As they move away from our phonics scheme book and become more independent readers, the selection of books for individuals is more nuanced.
Reading with children at home is incredibly important for their overall development. It strengthens their language skills, expanding their vocabulary and enhancing their understanding of grammar and sentence structure. Regular reading sessions help children develop a love for books and learning, fostering curiosity and imagination. It also improves their listening skills, as they learn to follow along with stories and comprehend complex ideas. Our aim is for children to read regularly at home with a target of 5 times a week.
Choosing the correct books
Reading books are assigned through a combination of methods designed to improve reading fluency, comprehension, and a love of reading. In Year 3, once the children are ready to move on from the phonics scheme, students are assessed for their reading fluency, which informs the selection of books appropriate for their level. Children are introduced and assigned books from the Accelerated Reader program. The Accelerated Reader assessment helps to monitor progress and assigns books that align with their reading abilities, allowing them to continue advancing through appropriate levels. This approach is maintained through Years 5 and 6, ensuring that students develop both their reading skills and a sustained interest in reading.
Reading Comprehension
'Reading is a complex, problem solving exercise. It does not come instinctively but needs to be carefully taught, applied and nurtured.’ (EEF)
Good comprehension draws from linguistic knowledge (of vocabulary and grammar) and on knowledge of the world. Comprehension skills develop through pupils’ experience of high-quality discussion with the teacher, as well as from reading and discussing a range of stories, poems and non-fiction. At Redmarley, we use a Quality Text Reading Approach ( Drawing Club and Curious Quests in EYFS and KS1 and DERIC in Ks2). This approach supports a deeper understanding of the whole curriculum, with texts carefully chosen and intentionally planned to enhance the learning at a cross curricular level.
A Positive Reading Culture
Children have opportunity to share stories and read alone and listen to stories which develops good reading for pleasure habits in class and at home. We have reading areas (mini libraries) which are accessible and engaging to children. We are always looking out for quality texts that appeal to children, so that they can become more 'hooked' and enthusiastic about reading and so the reading areas continue to engage. Children are heard read regularly at Redmarley, so that adults can gauge levels of fluency and to support further where necessary.
Reading for Pleasure
‘Reading for pleasure is the single most important indicator of a child’s success’ (OECD 2002).
‘The will influences the skill and vice versa’ (OECD 2010).
It is essential that children to read, as it is this that will drive them forward as readers. There are huge links between being a good reader and success in learning across the curriculum. It is our aim to encourage and nurture our developing readers by ensuring they have a great selection of exciting and stimulating texts to choose from. We highly value reading for pleasure.
For those children with additional needs or those find reading challenging:
We regularly assess reading against the National Curriculum and use reading fluency and phonics assessments to support us in understanding where children have gaps in reading. We then use these to inform our next steps and what needs to be put in place to support children to keep up and make good progress. Some of the ways we do this are:

Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
English Writing
How we Teach Writing at Redmarley
At Redmarley Primary Academy, our intent for Writing is to give children a purpose to write, through a thematic approach that engages and excites children on a topic e.g. Romans or Arctic Explorers. It provides a hook to learning, sparking children’s interest as writers, giving them a sense of purpose and audience and enabling them to write from a point of acquired knowledge e.g. biographies from Ernest Shackleton or diary extracts from a Roman soldier. This supports a richness and depth of writing, with more of an investment seen by learners, who are motivated and enabled to 'Shine as a Light in the World'. It is important to note, that teachers will divert at times from what is planned if an opportunity arises linked to an event of cultural significance or of current value e.g. children wrote as persuasive writers, presenting and performing speeches to be considered for the role of school House Captain. Our Curriculum is planned to ensure that we teach the breadth of the National Curriculum for Writing.
Our core drivers for Writing are:
To us Communication is at the heart of writing. In order to be a good writer and be able to communicate through this medium you need to:
To enable our children to connect with the purpose for writing as a means to communication we plan our writing around core texts (most often linked to theme). This provides a clear purpose for writing through oracy opportunities, learning outcomes, a published piece, as well as the grammar and punctuation rules and conventions being taught. This is all explicitly planned in our Writing Text Progression.
We prioritise this through our focus on quality adult-child interactions in early years and throughout Ks1 through our Continuous provision approach. Adults skilfully support and scaffold communication, building on vocabulary through strong discussion and deliberate enhancements. Across school we provide intentional opportunities for oracy e.g. through Collective Worship, as part of PQ Oracy Competition and throughout the school curriculum (children have a clear voice on topics, debating and discussing at a class level).
In Early Years and KS1, children are taught spelling as part of Little Wandle Phonics. Year 1 and 2 continue with this phonics scheme, transitioning to spelling once phonics completion is achieved. There’s a bridge to spelling program within Little Wandle, which continues into the first term of Year 3 to ease the transition from KS1 to KS2.
In KS2, Spelling is taught discretely and children then have the opportunity to practise and apply. Lower KS2 (Years 3 and 4) use worksheets to practise spelling, often revisiting KS1 coverage as well as teaching the new spelling rules within the curriculum. Upper KS2 (Years 5 and 6) have personalised spelling worksheets and assigned tasks, to accommodate individual learning needs, ensuring that spelling practise is targeted and impactful.
Spelling Assessment:
Spelling is assessed through teacher judgment based on students' independent writing. There’s no formal testing, but spellings are evaluated as part of written tasks.
This approach blends phonics, teacher judgment, and personalised tasks to help students improve their spelling. The transition between phonics and spelling, especially with the Little Wandle scheme, ensures continuity and support as students move from one stage to the next.
Grammar and Punctuation:
Grammar rules are taught explicitly through our text based curriculum, whereby teachers use our writing progression to enable children to learn the correct conventions matched to the text they are immersed in e.g. if the quality text is ‘What the Ladybird Heard’ by Julia Donaldson in Y1, then you would be learning to add in appropriate adjectives to make your character description sentences more interesting to the reader. The grammar progression for each national curriculum year is shared below.
Handwriting: We teach children to form the letters accurately to write words in a non-cursive script from Reception through to the end of year 2. We then introduce cursive script from Y3 upwards. All children are taught using the Little Wandle Handwriting Approach, however we recognise that some children have significant barriers in fine motor development. With this in mind we support the communication element of writing using technology and word processing software e.g. Clicker.

pageCache.text:
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
Geography
At RPA it is our intention that our coverage of the humanities subjects will provide children with a broad range of knowledge across History, Geography and RE. Our curriculum has been designed to link, where possible, our foundation subjects into termly themes, which allow our learners to link to our teaching of English and Reading and fully immerse their children into key ideas. We hope that our curriculum for the humanities subjects has been designed in such a way that the children are able to learn both knowledge and skills which will help them to progress as learners. We intend for the children to learn both about religions and history, but also to support them to form their own ideas and to learn from it, through discussion and investigation.
The result of our teaching is that our children will leave Redmarley with a strong understanding of both the skills and knowledge set out in the National Curriculum for the foundation subjects. In addition, that they can form opinions based on facts learned, and apply broader skills to other areas of their learning, such as investigation and discussion of sources.
Our foundation subjects offer our learners an opportunity to learn about the wider world, and the impact of key events on our current society. They are able to discuss historical events with respect and compassion and make links between their learning.
It is our clear aim that the children will gain a broad knowledge, but also learn the skills to think independently and assess information given so that they are able to form their own opinions.
Redmarley Church Of England Primary School
